key_insight: A deep learning surrogate can replace expensive CPFE simulations to optimize polycrystalline microstructures for competing quasi-static and dynamic strength targets.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, physically informed design of microstructures for impact-resistant materials while preserving full-field response information needed for engineering decisions.
method: Train a 3D U-Net to map 3D copper microstructures directly to full-field velocity histories from plate-impact simulations.
Couple the surrogate with stochastic microstructure generation and derivative-free optimization to search the design space.
Use a distribution-consistent reliability region (DCRR) based on MMD to monitor when optimization moves beyond the training distribution.
evidence_signal: Across multiple optimization cases, CPFE validation showed less than 3% prediction error, and surrogate-driven optimization cut cumulative evaluation time by about four orders of magnitude.
watch_item: Reliability depends on staying within or near the surrogate’s training distribution, so distribution shift must be monitored during optimization.
paper_title: Deep learning driven framework for optimization of polycrystalline microstructures under competing strength requirements
